Alice: Heads up — p95 for route chat/fast jumped ~40% since yesterday's runtime kernel change. Seeing ~220ms -> ~310ms. Also KV cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 78% on that route. Anyone digging in? /cc @Ben @Carla :thinking:
Ben: I rolled fused-attn v2 selection yesterday; fallback paths could add extra overhead for short sequences. Batcher logs also show bigger microbatches forming because token budgets are global. I think we need SLO-driven token budgets per route/tier to avoid long waits for low-latency routes.
Carla: Agreed. Quick proposal: per-route p95 target -> compute token_budget = floor(median_seq_len * multiplier * safety_factor). Start conservative: safety_factor fast=0.6, standard=0.85, bulk=1.1. This should reduce microbatch wait time for "fast" tier.
Nate: Profiling shows kernel fallback adds ~3-5ms when it happens, but the dominant cost is queueing. Snapshot: ```queue_stats: total_batches=482 avg_wait_ms=12 p95_wait_ms=86 max_wait_ms=220 token_budget_global=2048 avg_batch_size=7``` Long tail requests holding batches open.
Sam: Can try dynamic token-slicing: allow the batcher to split long requests into slices so they don't block others. slice_size = min(remaining_tokens, route_budget). Also change queue policy to prioritize low-latency tiers while still preserving fairness.
Ben: Plan for a canary: (1) add per-route token_budget configs, (2) introduce queue policy "tiered-priority" that de-prioritizes very large requests when p95 approaching SLO, (3) enable token-slicing for oversized requests. Canary on dedicated eng-runtime pool. Any objections?
Alice: No objections. Please add correctness checks so we don't truncate outputs unexpectedly. Add a focused eval set for chat/fast to validate generation continuity.
Carla: I'll draft the rollout doc and dashboard. Key metrics: p95 latency by route, KV hit rate by route, avg batch size, fallback_kernel_rate, token_slices_per_min, percent_requests_sliced.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: canary-id=canary-2027-03-15-01 route=chat/fast pool=dedicated-eng-runtime status=initiated :rocket:
Nate: Quick canary results after 10m warmup: p95 dropped from 310ms -> 260ms. avg_batch_size down from 7 -> 5. KV hit rate still ~79%. token_slices_count=48.
Sam: KV hit not recovered — hypothesis: slicing increases unique prefix patterns, causing more transient entries and evictions. Need to instrument prefix_reuse_rate and eviction_rate.
Ben: Good call. I'll keep kernel selection as-is for canary but toggle fallback threshold down if we see regressions. If p95 improves >10% and correctness tests pass, promote. Rollback window = 30m.
Alice: Sounds good. Please post follow-up after 1h and tag @oncall if p95 slips back above SLO. Thanks all.
